ostrzezenia.tekst: Carrot is a vegetable, and all fresh vegetables except most tomatoes are low-acid foods with a pH above 4.6.
Do not change the proportions of vinegar, vegetables and water and do not use vinegar of unknown acidity; use only recipes with tested proportions.
Low-acid foods, with a pH above 4.6, such as beets, cannot be safely canned in a boiling-water bath unless they are acidified according to a tested recipe.

akapity: The FDA list gives carrots a pH of about 5.88–6.40.
The FDA list gives peppers a pH of about 4.65–5.45.
NCHFP has a tested recipe for pickled carrots, but it contains carrots only, without peppers.
Most mixtures of low-acid and acid foods have a pH above 4.6 unless the recipe contains enough lemon juice, citric acid or vinegar.
The whole product needs a minimum, uniform level of acid to prevent the growth of botulism bacteria.
JarAtlas has found no tested recipe for carrots pickled together with jalapeño peppers from a checked source.
